title: Options are a risk overlay, not an engine of growth
summary: Like hedge funds, options are a tool, not an asset class. They do not create growth by themselves. The speaker's order: define your risk first, invest second, and use option overlays third to fine-tune the risk of the portfolio.

steps.caption: Step 1: define your risk. Decide the most the portfolio can lose before you pick any position.
Step 2: invest. Core holdings in asset classes are the engine of growth.
Step 3: a small options overlay fine-tunes the risk. It shapes the payoff; it is not the source of return.
Cash keeps dry powder and limits total exposure.
Risk first, invest second, overlay third.

takeaways: Hedge funds and options are tools to access asset classes, not asset classes.
Define risk first, invest second, use option overlays third.
Options fine-tune portfolio risk; they are not the engine of growth.
caveats: The clip ends with a website promotion.
Allocation numbers are illustrative; the speaker gives none.
